# Learned combiner (experimental)

**Not used for the Trust score; post-freeze; cross-validated on the same data the rules were frozen against, not a fresh held-out test.** Generated by `benchmark/ml_combiner.py` from `benchmark/results/run2/ml_*.csv`; no number in this file is typed by hand.

## What it is

A simple model that combines the frozen ruleset's own outputs for each item (finding counts per detector and tier, capability counts) into one score, to see whether a learned combination separates known-bad from random known-good packages better than the rules' fixed operating points. The rules, detectors, Trust score and verdicts are unchanged; the app never uses this model.

## Headline (feature set A_strict, logistic regression)

- ROC AUC 0.746 (95% CI 0.693-0.795).
- Recall 6.9% (95% CI 4.5%-9.7%) at a realized 0.2% false-positive rate (target 0%).
- Recall 29.2% (95% CI 24.1%-34.0%) at a realized 3.9% false-positive rate (target 5%).
- Recall 67.5% (95% CI 62.3%-72.6%) at a realized 14.2% false-positive rate (target 15%).
- Frozen rules: strict: 12.4% (39/314) at 0/117 false positives (0.0%); lenient: 50.0% (157/314) at 17/117 false positives (14.5%).

## Method

- Data: benchmark run 2, `benchmark/results/run2/features.csv` (from `benchmark/extract_features.py`): 314 scored known-bad (positives) vs 117 random known-good (negatives); scary and dormant items only scored, by models trained on all positives and negatives.
- Models with fixed default hyperparameters (nothing tuned): logistic regression on standardized features (main, coefficients below) and a random forest (comparison).
- Stratified 5-fold cross-validation repeated 5 times with fixed seeds; every item is scored only by models that did not train on it. Thresholds for the fixed false-positive rates are chosen inside each training fold (inner cross-validation on its known-good items), never on the test fold; the realized false-positive rate is reported. 95% intervals: stratified bootstrap over items.
- Feature sets: A-strict: detector/capability features without source indicators (headline); A: detector/capability features; B: A + install hook + inflated version; C: B + size, file count, artifact kind, ecosystem (not trusted: dataset bias).

## Source leakage check

Nearly every scored known-bad item is a DataDog sample and every random known-good item is a registry archive, so a feature that only one source can produce is a shortcut. Of 34 set-A features, 12 were excluded as source indicators (A-strict), from the detectors ci_workflow, committed_binary, dependency_injection, publisher_change, release_delta, revival_takeover: they need release history (not applicable to DataDog samples) or are non-zero only in registry archives. 10 features are non-zero only in DataDog samples; because almost every positive is a DataDog sample, they cannot be told apart from real malware signals and were kept. Full table: `benchmark/results/run2/ml_leakage.csv`. Feature set C (size, file count, artifact kind, ecosystem) mostly encodes the source and is **not trusted**.

## Sanity checks

- Ceiling, feature set A_strict: 53 of 314 known-bad items have an all-zero feature vector; 77 of 117 known-good are all-zero too; at 0% FP at most 261 of 314 known-bad can be ranked above them.
- Ceiling, feature set A: 53 of 314 known-bad items have an all-zero feature vector; 71 of 117 known-good are all-zero too; at 0% FP at most 261 of 314 known-bad can be ranked above them.
- Ceiling, feature set B: 39 of 314 known-bad items have an all-zero feature vector; 70 of 117 known-good are all-zero too; at 0% FP at most 275 of 314 known-bad can be ranked above them.
- Ceiling, feature set C: 0 of 314 known-bad items have an all-zero feature vector; 0 of 117 known-good are all-zero too; at 0% FP at most 314 of 314 known-bad can be ranked above them.
- Shuffled labels, feature set A_strict: ROC AUC 0.457 (95% CI 0.398-0.524); should be near 0.5.
- Shuffled labels, feature set A: ROC AUC 0.468 (95% CI 0.407-0.533); should be near 0.5.

## Caveats

- Cross-validated on the same 431 items the rules were frozen against: not a fresh held-out test.
- Class ratio 314 : 117, not real-world prevalence; precision is not reported for that reason.
- Dataset bias: known-bad items are DataDog samples (inert text), known-good items registry archives; set C shows how a model exploits that. Even A-strict may keep source effects that this data cannot separate.
- Post-freeze, unvalidated, never used for the Trust score or any verdict.
